briefFidelity: FAIL, and the gate closes here. The brief asks for fine linework throughout, delicate rather than heavy, with the drawing carried IN LINE RATHER THAN IN MASS. Before I had read a word of it I wrote that there is no line work, no stroke, no texture and no gradient anywhere — everything is a filled shape with alpha, and the only visible internal structure is alpha banding where fills overlap. That is not a shortfall, it is the inversion of the instruction, and it is true of all twelve seeds without exception. The second structural demand fails the same way: the brief wants a stem that divides, and divides again, each division smaller and turned slightly from the last. There is no branching anywhere in the twelve. What exists is a vertical chain of overlapping discs (9011, 9369, 10264, 10801) with a single non-recursive radial fan of triangles around it — one level, no descent, no diminution, no rotation of a child off a parent. Nothing in 9727, 10443 or 10980 divides. Third, 'botanical abstraction, the suggestion of a frond unfurling': blind, I read this work as a burr, a thistle head, a caterpillar, a torn-paper splat and a circular sawblade, and I read 10085 as a chevron. I did not once read a frond, and the cream-dominant seeds 9906, 10622, 10443 and 10980 read as aggressive and industrial, which is the opposite pole from delicate botanical growth. The palette instruction (moss and bone over a dark ground) is met exactly and is the one clause the work honours.
composition: Split, and the split tracks the same one variable everything else does. In the balanced seeds — 9011, 9369, 10264 and 9727 — there is real focal hierarchy: the green disc column is the subject, the cream spines are subordinate fringe, and the eye goes to the body first. That is the most convincing version of the object. In 9906, 10443, 10622 and 10980 the hierarchy inverts without intent: the triangles grow until they merge into a near-solid cream field covering most of the tile and the green collapses to an incidental kernel, so the frame reads as one undifferentiated pale mass rather than as a composed figure. 10801 has no hierarchy at all — a single green blob stack, one value, nothing to look at second. The frame is not used: the 512px single floats its subject dead centre with roughly half the canvas empty on all four sides, while 9906, 10443, 10622, 10980 and 10801 collide with the tile bounds instead. The work either ignores the edge or is cut by it; it never composes against it.
collectionCoherence: This is the strongest axis and it clearly passes as far as it goes. All twelve share one ground value, one green family, one cream, and exactly two shape primitives assembled by one rule — a disc column with radial wedges. Nothing appears in 10980 that is not also the material of 9190. The strain is at the two ends: 10801 carries no triangles at all and so is missing half the vocabulary, and 9906 has buried its greens so thoroughly that only a dot survives, so it is missing the other half. Those two read as the same project mainly because the ground and the green are identical, not because the drawing logic is legible in them. Eight of the twelve — 9011, 9369, 9548, 9190, 9727, 10264, 10443, 10980 — cohere without argument.
palette: Chosen, and correct against the brief: moss green and bone cream over a near-black ground, with a charcoal grey behind the cream wedges. No third hue appears in twelve seeds and three states, which is discipline rather than poverty, and the near-black ground supports the drawing rather than competing with it. The contrast range does uneven work, though. Cream on black is the only strong contrast in the piece and it carries almost everything, which is why the spike scale dominates every other reading. Green on black is mid-contrast and holds. The dark backing discs sit so close to the ground that they are nearly invisible, so the seeds that lean on them — 9548 above all, and 9190 — go faint and nearly drop out at browse size. The palette is right; the value structure inside it is thin.
seedVariation: It fails in both directions at once, which is unusual and worth naming precisely. Along most of the range these are one work at twelve settings of a single slider — triangle scale relative to disc scale. 9011, 9369 and 10264 are the same object at three near-identical settings; 9906, 10443, 10622 and 10980 are the same object at four near-identical settings further along. That is not twelve works. Then at the ends the same slider goes so far that cohesion breaks: 10801, with zero triangles, and 9906, with a cream field and a green dot, do not read as the same project as each other at all. Nothing else varies — no change of rule, no change of structure, no second axis of difference. The brief asks that tokens differ in how far the growth has gone; what actually differs is how large the thorns are, and past a point more thorn does not read as more growth, it reads as a different and more violent object.
thumbnailSurvival: Weak. Judging only the 120px sheets: the archetypes survive — you can tell a green column from a cream splat from a bare blob — but within-type resolution collapses and twelve tokens resolve to about four or five distinguishable things. 9906, 10443, 10622 and 10980 become one repeated stamp, a pale ragged mass with a green dot in it, and I could not reliably tell them apart at that size. 9011, 9369 and 10264 likewise converge on a single green-column-with-fringe. 9548 nearly vanishes: dim green and near-invisible backing discs on black, with too little cream to carry it. Only 10801 and 10085 stay individual at browse size, and they do so by being the two outliers. The small triangles also lose their points entirely at 120, so the one gesture that could have suggested fineness turns into a soft ragged edge.
marketResponse: Real but not the claimed change, and not reliably visible. What actually happens across neutral, stress and recovery on 9011, 9369, 9190 and 9548 is that recovery grows the discs larger and more opaque and brings the spines back brighter, whiter, longer and more numerous, while stress reduces the spine count, greys them toward charcoal, blunts them and flattens the discs toward one value. On 9011 and 9369 that is clearly visible at 120px — the recovery burr is furrier and more brilliant. On 9190 it is marginal. On 9548 the three states read as the same picture at 120 and very nearly the same at 256, so for that token the response has not been delivered. Against the brief the direction is coincidentally right and the substance is absent: recovery is meant to extend the branching and multiply its divisions, but there is no branching to extend, only more thorns on the same body; stress is meant to retract the form back toward a bare armature, and no armature is ever exposed — 9011 and 9369 under stress are the same solid blob stack, slightly duller. Stress is a de-tuned neutral, not a retraction.
tokenIdentity: Strong, and the best-executed axis in the set. Across all three states, 9011, 9190, 9369 and 9548 each keep their disc count, their disc positions, their overall silhouette and their placement in the frame. Nothing is re-rolled, nothing is substituted, and 9011 under stress is unmistakably the same object as 9011 under recovery despite the spines thinning and greying. The change reads as one thing under different conditions rather than as a replacement, which is exactly what is wanted. 9548 preserves identity so completely that it barely changes at all, so this axis and marketResponse pull against each other there.
artifacts: Several, and they read as accident rather than intent. Hard flat cuts at the tile boundary: 9011's top spine is sliced off the top edge, 9906 is cut at both top and bottom, 10443 and 10980 at the bottom, 10622 at bottom and left, and 10801's disc stack ends in a flat horizontal cut at the bottom edge. Heavy alpha banding wherever wedges overlap produces stepped grey facets — most visible in 9727, 10443 and 10980 where charcoal triangles sit beneath cream ones — which looks like stacked transparency rather than drawn shading. In 9906 and 10622 the cream mass has swallowed its own internal structure so the constituent triangles are legible only at the silhouette. No shape carries a stroke, so nothing has a drawn edge, and at 120px the smaller triangle tips disappear into mush. 9548's backing discs sit so near the ground value that parts of the token effectively vanish.
reasoning: The brief commissioned a frond: a botanical abstraction built from a stem that divides and divides again, each division smaller and turned from the last, drawn in fine line rather than in mass, delicate rather than heavy. Blind, before I had read any of that, I described a work with no stroke anywhere, made entirely of filled translucent discs and triangles, whose recurring reading was a burr, a thistle, a caterpillar, a torn-paper splat and a sawblade, and in which nothing divides. Those are not near-misses on the same object; they are the inverse of the two load-bearing clauses in the brief — line versus mass, and recursive division versus a single non-recursive radial fan. The palette is honoured exactly and token identity across states is genuinely well handled, and I want to be clear that I am not refusing this for being a different good artwork than the one asked for out of preference: I am refusing it because it is not the artwork that was asked for, on the axis the brief made central. Independent of the gate the work also has real weaknesses — the seed variation runs on one slider so twelve tokens resolve to four or five things at browse size, 9548's states are indistinguishable at 120px, and six of the twelve are cut by their own frame — but none of those decided it. The gate did.
wouldChange: Build the form from an actual recursive rule instead of a stack plus a fan: a root segment that spawns two or three children, each scaled down by a fixed ratio and rotated a few degrees off its parent, recursing three or four levels, so that depth of recursion is the thing that varies per seed and 'how far the growth has gone' becomes literal and legible. Draw it in stroke — thin bone-coloured polylines with the weight tapering as the recursion descends — and let mass appear only as sparse small fills at the tips, so the drawing is carried in line as commissioned. Bind stress to recursion DEPTH rather than to spine brightness, so stress genuinely prunes back to a bare two-level armature and recovery pushes to four or five levels with new divisions appearing; that alone would make 9548's states separable at 120px, where they are currently identical. Keep the moss-and-bone-on-black palette unchanged, it is right. Then cap the form's bounding box to leave a real margin so 9906, 10443, 10622, 10980 and 10801 stop colliding with the tile edge, and add a second variation axis — branching angle, or left/right asymmetry of division — so the twelve stop being one slider and start being twelve growths.
